# Policy history + rollback

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:policy-versioning` · **Epic:** [#41](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/41) · **Tickets:** 6 (2S 4M)

Policy and distributed settings move from in-place edits of the served YAML into an append-only versioned store in CP state. Every save creates a new version with author and message, admins can diff any two versions and roll back, and workers are always served the head version. The feature is behind `--policy-store=versioned` (default `file`), credential values are never stored in versions, and the served YAML is kept as a mirror of head so turning the flag off or downgrading the binary serves the same policy.

## How we build it

- Gate: new `warden control-plane --policy-store=file|versioned` flag, default `file`. `versioned` requires `--state-dir` and the cpstate DB from W-P1-SSO-01, and fails at startup with an actionable error without them. In `file` mode, or with no state dir, the CP keeps today's YAML serve, edit and 3s re-read path byte-for-byte. The default can flip in a later release once the whole feature has shipped.
- Schema (cpstate migrations): `policy_versions(version INTEGER PK, parent_version, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind (the W-P1-AAUD-01 auth_method set: oidc|breakglass|cli|none|system), message <=512 chars, source[policy|settings|llmproviders|rollback|import], doc_json, doc_sha256)`, a one-row `policy_head(version)`, and an append-only `policy_publish_log(seq INTEGER PK, version, etag, reason, actor_sub, at)` written in the same transaction as every head move. No code path updates or deletes version rows. Later features use publish_log: signed bundles take seq as their monotonic number, explain resolves a timestamp to a version, and the CP appends a row whenever the served ETag changes without a new version (block-list edits from W-P1-BLOCK-03, AWS credential rotation), so ETag-to-version lookups never miss.
- doc_json is the canonical policyWire {allowlist, denylist, settings}. Credential values are never versioned: a non-empty `settings.secrets.secretAccessKey` (internal/config/settings.go, the sanctioned credential-on-wire exception) is replaced by `sha256:<16 hex>` before hashing and storing. The live value stays in the CP-local served YAML secretStore block, as today, and is overlaid when the served wire is built, so /policy bytes and the worker behaviour are unchanged. `blockedUsers` (W-P1-BLOCK-01) is also excluded from doc_json and merged in at serve time, so rollback can never unblock a user. The /policy ETag is the hash of the merged served wire, not doc_sha256.
- `PolicyVersionStore` is an interface (Create, Head, Get, List, PublishLog) with a SQLite implementation so a later Postgres store can implement it. Create is one transaction: insert the version, `UPDATE policy_head SET version=new WHERE version=expectedHead` (0 rows means ErrConflict and rollback of the transaction), append the publish_log row. This compare-and-swap works across processes, so the CLI and the CP cannot both create the same version. A doc whose doc_sha256 equals head's writes nothing and returns changed=false. Ordering always uses the version integer, never created_at.
- Validation reuses the existing full loader, not a parallel validator: render the candidate (served YAML root with its policy and settings blocks replaced by the doc, using the encoders WritePolicy/WriteSettings use today), write a temp file and run config.NewLocalYAMLProvider, the same check atomicWriteConfig makes. This enforces default-deny (empty allowlist rejected), domain and rate-limit checks and cross-block references such as judge/explore llmProvider. Save, import and rollback all go through it, and a failure returns 422 with the loader error and leaves head unchanged.
- One publish path: `s.publish(ctx, mutate func(*policyWire), expectedHead, msg, source)` runs under writeMu. WritePolicy (allow/deny), WriteSettings (the blocks its form owns) and WriteLLMProviders (llmProviders) each change only their own fields and carry every other wire field from head (dlp, advisory, explore and so on). CP-local writers (WriteIntegrations, WriteDetection, console) keep the YAML round-trip. A test asserts every SettingsWire field is either owned by a writer or carried.
- Serving: policyServer.loadPolicy returns head doc plus credential overlay plus blockedUsers, held in the in-memory policyWatch. The /policy hot path never touches the DB. Create calls Refresh so long-poll waiters wake at once. In versioned mode the existing 3s ticker runs `SELECT version FROM policy_head` and reloads the doc only when the version changes, so out-of-process writes (CLI) reach workers within 3s plus one long-poll cycle.
- Degraded modes: startup in versioned mode is fail-closed. If the store cannot be read, head points at a missing version, or a doc fails its doc_sha256 check, the CP refuses to start with an actionable error and never falls back to the possibly older YAML. A runtime read error keeps last-known-good in memory (as policyWatch does today) and logs. Workers are unaffected: they keep last-known-good.
- Write-through mirror: after every head move, the CP renders head's policy and settings blocks into the served YAML through atomicWriteConfig and records the mirrored file hash. The YAML therefore always equals head, which makes `--policy-store=file` or a binary downgrade serve the same policy. A mirror failure (for example a read-only mount) logs at error and never fails the version. If the ticker finds the YAML blocks differ from the mirrored hash, that is an external edit: log a warning once per distinct file hash, show a dashboard banner, keep serving head. External edits come back in through `warden policy import`.
- Migration: in versioned mode with an empty store, the CP imports the served YAML's allow/deny and config.SettingsWireFromPolicy (credential redacted) as version 1, author `system:import`, and checks that the served /policy bytes and ETag are unchanged. It is idempotent: a non-empty store is never re-imported.
- Concurrency contract: GET /dashboard/api/policy and /dashboard/api/settings return `version` in the body and an `X-Warden-Policy-Version: N` header. Writes send `If-Match: "v<N>"`. A stale value returns 409 `{error:"policy_conflict", head, author}` (409, not 412, so the body can name the conflicting author). Policy, settings and llmProviders share one head, so a settings save makes a concurrent allow/deny save conflict. Missing If-Match is accepted until W-P1-PVER-04 makes the UI always send it, then returns 428 in versioned mode. /policy's content-hash ETag is unchanged.
- Authors: OIDC sessions record sub and email from the request Principal (W-P1-SSO-04). console.auth none records `anonymous` with author_kind none; a break-glass session records `breakglass:<username>` with author_kind breakglass. Migration records `system:import`. The CLI records `cli:<os user>`. Messages are capped at 512 characters with control characters stripped.
- Rollback to N creates version latest+1 with N's doc, source `rollback`, message `rollback to v<N>` plus an optional user note. It requires If-Match, is revalidated against today's rules (422 if N no longer validates), and keeps the current credential and block list. History is never rewritten.
- Diff is structural. Allow and deny lists are multisets keyed by a new `diffKey()` method on config.AllowlistEntry and config.DenylistEntry, which today returns domain|port (rateLimit and timeWindow are compared attributes, duplicates show as count changes). W-P1-GPOL-01 extends diffKey when it adds groups/users. Settings are compared by JSON path into {added, removed, changed}, and credential paths only ever show fingerprints.
- Audit and observability: each save, rollback, import and migration writes an admin audit row with target `policy` and before/after `v<N>:<doc_sha256>`, through a `policy` StateHasher for HTTP paths (W-P1-AAUD-02) and direct appends for migration and CLI. slog `policy version created` carries version, parent, source, author_sub and doc_sha256, never doc content or settings values. The fleet view shows each worker's version by mapping its heartbeat ETag through policy_publish_log. Metrics hooks (head version, store errors) are noted for when CP metrics exist. P1 has no pruning; growth is one row per save.

## Done when

On a CP started with `--state-dir` and `--policy-store=versioned`, an existing deployment upgrades and serves byte-identical /policy JSON as version 1. Editors make three saves (policy, settings and llmProviders), each shown as a version with author, message and a structural diff, and a concurrent stale save gets 409. Rolling back to version 1 creates version 5, workers pull it within one long-poll cycle, and the fleet view shows them on v5. The served YAML mirrors head, so restarting with `--policy-store=file` serves the same policy. The block list is unchanged by the rollback, every step has an admin audit row, and no policy_versions row or history API response contains a raw AWS secretAccessKey.

### 1/6 · W-P1-PVER-01

**Add versioned policy store and serve the head version**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#42](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/42)

Add the policy_versions, policy_head and policy_publish_log migrations and a PolicyVersionStore in internal/controlplane, plus the `--policy-store=file|versioned` flag (default `file`). In versioned mode, policyServer serves the head doc with the live AWS credential overlaid, and the 3s ticker polls the head version. Credential values are redacted before any row is written because the table is append-only. This ticket writes no versions on its own, so with an empty store or in file mode behaviour is unchanged.

**Requirements**

- Migrations create `policy_versions(version, parent_version, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind, message, source, doc_json, doc_sha256)`, `policy_head(version)` and `policy_publish_log(seq, version, etag, reason, actor_sub, at)`; the store exposes no update or delete of versions.
- Create(ctx, doc, author, msg, source, expectedHead) runs in one transaction with `UPDATE policy_head ... WHERE version=expectedHead` as a cross-process compare-and-swap; 0 rows returns ErrConflict and writes nothing; a doc equal to head returns changed=false and writes nothing.
- Before hashing and storing, a non-empty settings.secrets.secretAccessKey is replaced by `sha256:<16 hex>`; the live value is read from the served YAML secretStore block and overlaid only when building the served wire.
- Validation renders the doc into the served YAML root, writes a temp file and runs config.NewLocalYAMLProvider; no parallel validator is added.
- `--policy-store=versioned` without `--state-dir` fails at startup with an actionable error; in `file` mode, or versioned with an empty store, /policy is byte-identical to today.
- Startup in versioned mode fails closed when the store is unreadable, head points at a missing version, or doc_sha256 does not match; a runtime read error keeps last-known-good.
- The /policy hot path never reads the DB; the ETag stays etagFor(served wire); Create calls Refresh().
- slog `policy version created` logs version, parent, source, author_sub and doc_sha256 only; doc content, settings values and the credential are never logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add internal/controlplane/policystore.go (new): the cpstate migrations, the PolicyVersionStore interface, a SQLite implementation (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, CAS update, publish_log append) and ErrConflict.
2. Add redactCredentials/overlayCredentials (new) in policystore.go for Settings.Secrets.SecretAccessKey, reading the live value from the served YAML secretStore block.
3. Factor the block rendering out of Server.WritePolicy and Server.WriteSettings (controlplane.go) into renderDocToRoot (new) and add validateDoc (new), which reuses the temp-file and NewLocalYAMLProvider logic of atomicWriteConfig.
4. Change newPolicyServer and policyServer.loadPolicy (policyserver.go) to take an optional store: when it is set and Head() > 0, decode doc_json, check doc_sha256, overlay the credential and return it; otherwise keep the YAML path. Cache the head version so Refresh reloads the doc only when it changes.
5. Add the `--policy-store` flag in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go and a PolicyStore field (new) on controlplane.Config; in Server.Start, when versioned, make the policyReloadInterval ticker poll the head version instead of re-reading YAML.
6. Add tests in internal/controlplane/policystore_test.go (new) and extend controlplane_test.go for file-mode and empty-store byte identity.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given head v3, Create with expectedHead=2 returns ErrConflict, the row count is unchanged and Head() is 3; with 20 goroutines racing Create on the same expectedHead under -race, exactly one succeeds.
- [ ] Given a doc with an invalid domain pattern or an empty allowlist, Create returns a validation error and Head() and the served ETag are unchanged.
- [ ] Given settings with secrets.secretAccessKey set, after Create the doc_json column and the DB file do not contain the raw value, while GET /policy still carries it.
- [ ] Given a long-poll waiter on the current ETag with wait=5s, Create with changed content wakes it with the new doc within 1s; Create with identical content writes no row and the ETag is unchanged.
- [ ] Given `--policy-store=file` (default), or versioned with an empty store, GET /policy is byte-identical to a CP built from main on the same files.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyVersionStore|TestPolicyServerVersioned'` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#18--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-PVER-02`](policy-versioning.md#26--w-p1-pver-02) Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish; [`W-P1-OPS1-04`](ops-hardening.md#44--w-p1-ops1-04) Add CP state-dir lock and verified restore command

### 2/6 · W-P1-PVER-02

**Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#43](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/43)

In versioned mode, import the served config as version 1 on first start, then route every writer of a wire-carried block (WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteLLMProviders) through one publish path that builds the new doc from head and creates a version. The dashboard writer setters gain context.Context so the author comes from the request Principal, and the dashboard GET/POST handlers carry the head version and If-Match. Without WriteLLMProviders in this path, provider edits would save but never reach workers.

**Requirements**

- With an empty store in versioned mode, import allow/deny plus config.SettingsWireFromPolicy (credential redacted) as version 1, author `system:import`, message `initial import from <path>`, and append an admin audit row directly; never re-import a non-empty store.
- Migration does not change the served wire: /policy bytes and ETag are identical before and after, so no worker reports `behind`.
- Add `s.publish(ctx, mutate, expectedHead, msg, source)` under writeMu; WritePolicy, WriteSettings and WriteLLMProviders change only the fields they own and carry every other wire field from head; WriteSettings keeps today's preserve-on-empty rule for secretAccessKey via the stored fingerprint.
- Dashboard setters take ctx and write metadata (`SetPolicyWriter(func(context.Context, config.Policy, WriteMeta) error)`, and likewise SetSettingsWriter and SetLLMProvidersWriter); author is Principal sub/email, or `anonymous` when console.auth is none.
- GET /dashboard/api/policy and /dashboard/api/settings return `version` and `X-Warden-Policy-Version`; a stale `If-Match: "v<N>"` returns 409 `{error:"policy_conflict", head, author}`; a missing If-Match is accepted for now so today's UI keeps working.
- Register a `policy` StateHasher with W-P1-AAUD-02 that returns `v<head>:<doc_sha256>`, replacing the built-in policy hasher in versioned mode, so HTTP saves record before and after.
- In file mode all writers keep today's YAML round-trip unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add importInitialVersion (new) in internal/controlplane/policystore.go, called from controlplane.New when the store is versioned and Head()==0; compare etagFor before and after and fail startup on mismatch.
2. Add Server.publish (new) in controlplane.go and rewrite Server.WritePolicy, Server.WriteSettings and Server.WriteLLMProviders (llmproviders_write.go) to call it in versioned mode, keeping refresh() and reinjectExploreLLM().
3. Change SetPolicyWriter, SetSettingsWriter and SetLLMProvidersWriter in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go to take ctx and WriteMeta (new: ifMatch, message); parse If-Match in putPolicy and putSettings and the llmproviders handler, map ErrConflict to 409 and add the version header and field to the GET responses.
4. Update the ConfigEditor interface in internal/controlplane/seams.go and the wiring at controlplane.go (dash.SetPolicyWriter, dash.SetSettingsWriter, dash.SetLLMProvidersWriter) for the new signatures.
5. Register the `policy` StateHasher in Server.Handler when versioned.
6. Add a field-ownership table test listing each SettingsWire field and its owning writer or 'carried', and update internal/dashboard/policy_edit_test.go, dashboard_llmproviders_test.go and internal/controlplane/llmproviders_write_test.go for the ctx setters.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a state dir with a populated config.yaml and an empty store, starting with `--policy-store=versioned` serves /policy byte-identical to file mode with the same ETag, and the store holds one version authored `system:import`.
- [ ] Given a session Principal {sub:u1, email:a@x}, POST /dashboard/api/policy with the current If-Match creates a version with author_sub=u1 and author_email=a@x; replaying it with the old If-Match returns 409 with head and author.
- [ ] Given a WriteLLMProviders edit in versioned mode, a new version with source `llmproviders` exists and GET /policy carries the new provider list.
- [ ] Given a WriteSettings edit, the dlp and advisory blocks of the new version equal head's (carried, not dropped).
- [ ] Given `--policy-store=file`, the existing internal/controlplane and internal/dashboard tests pass with only signature updates.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyMigrationByteIdentical|TestVersionedWriters|TestSettingsFieldOwnership'` and `go test ./internal/dashboard -run 'TestPolicyWrite|TestLLMProviders'` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-01`](policy-versioning.md#16--w-p1-pver-01) Add versioned policy store and serve the head version; [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#58--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route; [`W-P1-AAUD-02`](admin-audit-log.md#24--w-p1-aaud-02) Record CP admin mutations and logins through audit middleware

### 3/6 · W-P1-PVER-03

**Add policy history, structural diff and rollback APIs**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#44](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/44)

Add dashboard APIs to list versions, fetch one version, diff two versions and roll back, behind the W-P1-SSO-05 role table. The diff lives in a new internal/controlplane/policydiff.go and keys entries with a new diffKey() method so W-P1-GPOL-01 can extend it. Because internal/controlplane imports internal/dashboard, the handlers talk to the store through a new dashboard.PolicyHistory interface. Rollback creates a new version and never touches credentials or the block list.

**Requirements**

- GET /dashboard/api/policy/versions?cursor=&limit= returns metadata only (version, parent, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind, message, source, doc_sha256), newest first, default 50, max 200.
- GET /dashboard/api/policy/versions/{v} returns the doc with credentials shown only as fingerprints; GET .../versions/{v}/diff?against={u} defaults u to head.
- POST .../versions/{v}/rollback (editor, CSRF) requires If-Match, revalidates the target, and creates latest+1 with source `rollback` and message `rollback to v<N>` plus an optional note; content equal to head returns 200 with changed=false.
- Diff: allow and deny lists are multisets keyed by diffKey() (domain|port today); rateLimit/timeWindow differences are `changed`; settings are compared by JSON path into {added, removed, changed}; credential paths show only fingerprints.
- Every new route has an authz entry: GET viewer, POST rollback editor; denied attempts are audited by the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware.
- Errors: unknown v 404, non-integer v 400, stale If-Match 409, failed validation 422 with the loader error.
- Rollback logs from_head, to_version, new_head and actor_sub, never doc contents.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add diffKey() methods (new) on config.AllowlistEntry and config.DenylistEntry in internal/config/config.go.
2. Add internal/controlplane/policydiff.go (new): DiffDocs(a, b policyWire) PolicyDiff{Allow, Deny []EntryChange; Settings []PathChange} with occurrence counting for duplicates and generic JSON-map walking for settings.
3. Add the dashboard.PolicyHistory interface and SetPolicyHistory setter (new) in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go and register the four routes.
4. Add internal/controlplane/policyhistory.go (new): an adapter over PolicyVersionStore whose Rollback calls Server.publish with the target doc, and wire it in Server.Handler when versioned.
5. Add the four routes to the SSO-05 authz route table.
6. Add policydiff_test.go and policyhistory_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] policydiff_test.go covers allow added, removed and changed (rateLimit), duplicate entries as count changes, a deny change, a nested settings change (judge.model), and a secretAccessKey change shown only as a fingerprint change.
- [ ] Given versions 1 to 3, an editor POST /versions/1/rollback with If-Match "v3" gives head=4, version 4's doc_sha256 equals version 1's, and a worker long-polling /policy receives the new ETag within one wait cycle.
- [ ] Given a viewer session, list, get and diff return 200 and rollback returns 403 with an admin audit row outcome=denied.
- [ ] Given a rollback, admin audit holds one row with target=policy, before=`v3:<sha>` and after=`v4:<sha>`; no response body or log line contains the raw secretAccessKey and the blocked users list is unchanged.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyDiff|TestPolicyRollback|TestPolicyHistoryAPI'` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-02`](policy-versioning.md#26--w-p1-pver-02) Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish; [`W-P1-AAUD-02`](admin-audit-log.md#24--w-p1-aaud-02) Record CP admin mutations and logins through audit middleware

### 4/6 · W-P1-PVER-04

**Add history panel with diff view and rollback to dashboard**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#45](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/45)

In internal/dashboard/index.html, add a History panel to the policy tab that lists versions, shows the structural diff against head and offers rollback with a confirm dialog. The policy, settings and llmProviders save flows ask for an optional message and send If-Match; on 409 the UI reloads head and names the conflicting author. Once the UI always sends If-Match, the server returns 428 for a missing header in versioned mode.

**Requirements**

- The History panel shows only when GET /dashboard/api/policy returns `version`; it lists version, author email or sub, relative time and message, with cursor 'load more'.
- Selecting a version renders the /diff response (added, removed, changed with old and new); no client-side text diff.
- The rollback button is enabled only for editor or admin per /auth/me, and POSTs with X-Warden-CSRF (W-P1-SSO-04) and If-Match set to the current head.
- Save dialogs ask for an optional message (512 chars max) and send If-Match; on 409 the UI shows 'policy changed by <author> (v<N>)' and keeps the user's unsaved edits.
- Author and message are rendered only with textContent, never innerHTML; credential values are never shown.
- After this ticket, putPolicy, putSettings and the llmproviders handler return 428 for a missing If-Match in versioned mode; file mode is unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the History panel markup and fetch logic to the policy tab in internal/dashboard/index.html using the existing jget helper.
2. Add the diff view and rollback confirm dialog, sending the CSRF header from /auth/me and If-Match.
3. Change the policy save flow (around the existing PUT in index.html) and the settings and llmProviders save flows to send the message and If-Match and handle 409.
4. Make If-Match required (428) in versioned mode in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go.
5. Add Go tests in internal/dashboard/policy_edit_test.go against the served HTML and handlers.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] In versioned mode, GET /dashboard/ returns HTML containing the History container, a fetch of `/dashboard/api/policy/versions`, and rollback code that sets both `X-Warden-CSRF` and `If-Match`.
- [ ] A test checks the template assigns author and message only through textContent (no innerHTML for these fields).

### 5/6 · W-P1-PVER-05

**Mirror head into the served YAML and detect external edits**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#233](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/233)

After every head move in versioned mode, render head's policy and settings blocks back into the served YAML with atomicWriteConfig, so switching to `--policy-store=file` or downgrading the binary serves the same policy. When the YAML blocks no longer match the mirrored hash, treat it as an external edit: warn once, show a dashboard banner and keep serving head. Also show each worker's version number in the fleet view and document the feature.

**Requirements**

- After each successful publish, the CP writes head's policy and settings blocks (with the live credential, not the fingerprint) into the served YAML via atomicWriteConfig and records the mirrored file hash.
- A mirror failure logs at error with the version and never fails or rolls back the version.
- The ticker compares the YAML blocks with the mirrored hash and logs `served config policy block differs from head; ignored` once per distinct file hash, with file_sha256 and head.
- GET /dashboard/api/policy reports `drift: true` when an external edit is detected, and the UI shows a banner pointing to `warden policy import`.
- The fleet API reports each worker's policy version by mapping its heartbeat ETag through policy_publish_log; unknown ETags show as `unknown`.
- docs/control-plane.md documents the flag, migration, mirror, drift, If-Match contract and the downgrade path.
- Whenever the served ETag changes without a version create (a W-P1-BLOCK-03 block-list change or an AWS credential change), policyServer appends a policy_publish_log row with the current head version and reason `blocked_users` or `credential`, so the fleet lookup does not show an up-to-date worker as `unknown`.
- When admin audit is enabled, each newly detected external edit appends one admin_audit row through the Recorder (auth_method system, action config.external_change, target policy, before `v<head>:<doc_sha256>`, after `file:<file_sha256>`), once per distinct file hash.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add mirrorHead (new) in internal/controlplane/policystore.go, called by Server.publish after a successful Create, reusing renderDocToRoot and atomicWriteConfig.
2. Extend the versioned ticker in Server.Start to hash the served YAML blocks and compare with the mirrored hash.
3. Add the version lookup to the fleet view in controlplane.go (handleHeartbeat already records policyETag) using PolicyVersionStore.PublishLog, and add PolicyVersionStore.AppendPublish(ctx, etag, reason, actor) called from policyServer.Refresh when the ETag changes without a version create.
4. Add the drift field and banner to internal/dashboard/dashboard.go and index.html.
5. Update docs/control-plane.md.
6. Add tests in internal/controlplane/policymirror_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given versioned mode and three saves, the served YAML loaded with config.NewLocalYAMLProvider yields the same wire as head, and a CP restarted with `--policy-store=file` serves the same /policy bytes.
- [ ] Given the served YAML made read-only, a save still creates a version and one error line is logged.
- [ ] Given an external edit to the YAML policy block, /policy is unchanged after two ticker cycles, exactly one warning is logged, and GET /dashboard/api/policy returns drift=true.
- [ ] Given a worker heartbeat with the ETag of v2 while head is v4, the fleet API shows version 2 and behind=true.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyMirror|TestPolicyDrift|TestFleetPolicyVersion'` passes.
- [ ] Given a block-list change after v4, a worker heartbeating the new ETag shows version 4 (not unknown), and an external YAML edit with admin audit enabled writes exactly one config.external_change row: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestFleetPolicyVersionBlocklist|TestPolicyDriftAudited'`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-02`](policy-versioning.md#26--w-p1-pver-02) Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-AREG-04`](agent-registry.md#47--w-p2-areg-04) Serve registered agents in the policy wire; [`W-P2-SBND-02`](signed-bundles.md#27--w-p2-sbnd-02) Serve the signed bundle envelope on GET /policy behind --bundles; [`W-P3-PUL-08`](per-user-limits.md#810--w-p3-pul-08) Publish fleet cost blocks as costBlockedUsers from the control plane

### 6/6 · W-P1-PVER-06

**Add warden policy import and export commands**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#234](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/234)

Add `warden policy import` and `warden policy export` under the existing `warden policy` command so operators who manage policy as files can create versions and get a YAML out for downgrade, disaster recovery or GitOps hand-off. Import opens the cpstate DB directly and uses the same compare-and-swap Create as the CP, so a running CP picks the change up through head polling. CLI actions do not go through HTTP, so they append admin audit rows directly.

**Requirements**

- `warden policy import --state-dir <dir> --file <yaml> [--message m]` validates with the same validateDoc, redacts the credential, and calls Create with expectedHead = current head and author `cli:<os user>`.
- Import of content equal to head prints `no change` and exits 0; a conflict prints the new head and exits non-zero.
- Import appends an admin audit row with actor `cli:<os user>` and target `policy`.
- `warden policy export --state-dir <dir> [--version N]` writes a loadable config YAML (policy and settings blocks of that version, credential fingerprint left out) to stdout.
- Neither command prints credential values; errors name the file and loader message only.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add cmd/proxy/policy_import.go (new) with the import and export cobra commands, attached to the parent from newPolicyCmd in cmd/proxy/policy.go.
2. Expose the store constructor and validateDoc from internal/controlplane for CLI use (new exported wrappers).
3. Append the audit row through adminaudit.Store.Append from W-P1-AAUD-01, loading the key from `--admin-audit-key-file` (default `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`, never minting a new key when rows exist); skip with a one-line notice when the admin_audit table does not exist.
4. Add cmd/proxy/policy_import_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a CP running against a state dir and a worker long-polling with wait=30s, `warden policy import --state-dir <dir> --file new.yaml --message m` makes the worker receive the new ETag within 5s and adds an audit row with actor `cli:<user>`.
- [ ] Re-importing the same file prints `no change`, exits 0 and adds no version.
- [ ] `warden policy export --version 1` output loads with config.NewLocalYAMLProvider and contains no secretAccessKey value.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestPolicyImport|TestPolicyExport'` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-PVER-02`](policy-versioning.md#26--w-p1-pver-02) Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish; [`W-P1-AAUD-01`](admin-audit-log.md#14--w-p1-aaud-01) Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate
